items.headline: 美議員迫降湖面泳渡逃生
items.context: 美國聯邦眾議員湯姆·蒂芬尼（Tom Tiffany）搭乘的小型飛機，因機械故障被迫緊急迫降在威斯康辛州一座湖面。蒂芬尼隨後游泳上岸，僅受輕傷。
items.thread_text:

美國聯邦眾議員湯姆·蒂芬尼（Tom Tiffany）搭乘的小型飛機發生機械故障，飛行員被迫將飛機緊急迫降在威斯康辛州一座湖面上。

items.context: 土耳其警方近日突襲多間同志酒吧與LGBTQ+運動人士住所，拘留數十人。人權團體指控政府正以「家庭價值」為名，鎖定LGBTQ+社群進行打壓。

items.context: 威尼斯影展公布得獎名單，丹麥導演梅伊·圖基（May el-Toukhy）執導的《陌生女子》（Woman Unknown）奪下最高獎項，南韓導演李滄東的《可能的愛》（Possible Love）也獲獎。影展先前因入圍女導演比例偏低受到批評，這份得獎名單被認為多少挽回了形象。
items.thread_text:
威尼斯影展公布得獎名單

威尼斯影展公布得獎名單，丹麥導演梅伊·圖基（May el-Toukhy）執導的《陌生女子》（Woman Unknown）奪下最高獎項，故事描述二戰後艱困年代，一名丹麥女僕的遭遇。

items.thread_text:
倫敦巴黎藝文週記

這週西方藝文圈很熱鬧。法語天后席琳·狄翁（Celine Dion）在巴黎睽違多年重返舞台，儘管她仍在對抗僵人症候群，演出中一度激動落淚，但歌聲依然穩健有力，這場復出被形容為一次動人的凱旋。

多倫多影展這邊，兩屆奧斯卡影帝馬赫夏拉·阿里（Mahershala Ali）主演新片，飾演一名陷入悲傷的殺手，混合動作與家庭劇情，評論相當正面。

倫敦西區也有新戲登場。舞台劇《孩子們》（The Children）描寫兩位退休核能工程師，在一場災難性爆炸後被迫直面過去，劇評稱之為動人之作。同一週，逍遙音樂節（The Proms）壓軸夜也登場，近四小時的終場曲目橫跨古典到流行，場面熱鬧非凡。

sources.summary: Plenitude Arena, Paris Dion wiped away tears and belted out the notes, giving an astounding performance despite her diagnosis of stiff person syndrome In 2022, when Céline Dion shared that she had been diagnosed with a rare incurable neurological disorder called stiff person syndrome (SPS), there was no guarantee that the 58-year-old would ever tour again. Her condition, which resulted in muscle spasms so strong that it left her with broken ribs , had made it impossible to perform, and in a 2024 documentary, I Am: Céline Dion , fans saw how the disease had constricted her once seemingly infallible voice. Through it all, though, Dion was resolute that she would one day return to the stage. “If I can’t run, I’ll walk. If I can’t walk, I’ll crawl,” she said in the film. “But I won’t stop.” Thankfully at the opening night of her sold out five-week residency in Paris, her first full-length concerts in six years, no crawling is needed: Céline Dion is back. She glides on to the stage in a black dress, an enormous diamond necklace clasped around her throat, and launches into On ne change pas. There are tears almost immediately: she struggles through the second verse, her voice cracking as she begins to cry. By the time the strum of Destin has kicked in, though, that emotion is replaced with sheer elation. “I made a promise to be back on stage. Singing for you. Singing for me,” she says. “Singing for life.” Continue reading...
sources.title: Céline Dion review – singer’s first live show in years marks a triumphant, emotional return

sources.summary: Toronto film festival: the two-time Oscar-winner is an unusual killer in a compelling mix of pulpy action and family drama Latif, the solemn hitman played soulfully by Mahershala Ali, carries diapers in his kill kit. I can’t tell if that’s because they come in handy when soaking up pools of blood on the fly; or because at a moment’s notice the hitman has to switch over from his brutal occupation to daddy duties. Or perhaps it’s both for this contract killer who comes armed with a blade and baby wipes, who takes lives and nurtures them, whose life is composed of jarring and poetic contradictions, much like the movie he’s in. Those contradictions are on full striking display in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’s opening moments, an explosive close-quarters brawl in a restroom, after which Latif uses the baby wipes to clean up the mess he made with that blade. It’s a lovely image, in a film filled with so many, cutting right through the tension within this character. It also feels like a wink to the audience from Ali and writer/director Bassam Tariq, a way for them to acknowledge right off the top the distracting mess made by that other Blade. Continue reading...

sources.summary: Lyric Hammersmith, London A catastrophic explosion forces retired nuclear engineers Syal and Declan Conlon to confront their past after a visit by Kerry Fox in this revival of Lucy Kirkwood’s debut Ten years on from its powerful debut , Lucy Kirkwood’s clever and funny play feels just as potent – if not more so. There’s so much to admire and enjoy here: Kirkwood’s skilful and layered writing; Rachel O’Riordan’s precise and thoughtful direction; Gary McCann’s striking design and, above all, a trio of richly nuanced performances from three brilliant older actors: Meera Syal, Declan Conlon and Kerry Fox. For all the ideas about the legacy we leave behind for our children, I found myself reflecting on how much we still overlook our elders, and what a terrible failing and waste that is. O’Riordan’s softly rumbling production unfolds sometime in the near future (although that supposed future feels horribly close these days). There has been a catastrophic explosion at a nuclear power plant. Exclusion zones have been established and lives redrawn. Husband and wife, Robin and Hazel (who are both nuclear engineers), have retired to a nearby crumbling cottage. When old friend and fellow engineer, Rose, turns up unannounced – determined to lure them back to work at the power plant – all three are forced to confront painful mistakes from their past and think deeply about their futures. At Lyric Hammersmith , London, until 3 October. Continue reading...

sources.summary: Royal Albert Hall, London The evening features everything from a rendition of an inscrutable Samuel Barber concerto to a celebration of Dolly Parton, but the real star is tartan-clad tenor Nicky Spence In Richard Strauss’s Ariadne auf Naxos, a wealthy man commissions an evening’s entertainment: a lofty new opera and a comic burlesque. But when time constraints force them to be performed simultaneously, surreal musical chaos ensues. One can only assume that the BBC was taking notes. The Last Night of the Proms is the finale to eight weeks of concerts, and the BBC’s annual identity crisis. Is this the celebratory end to a season of serious music or a standalone party, whose first half is something to be endured before the real fun begins? It’s both, of course. And that’s where the trouble starts. Continue reading...

sources.summary: President has hyped growth of federal investment accounts to help US children – for his own political gain Since returning to the White House, Donald Trump has scrapped rules that made childcare more affordable and pushed to cut funding for the nation’s public schools . But with midterm elections fast approaching and his approval ratings very low, the US president has repeatedly trumpeted a two-month-old program designed to help the nation’s children. That program, unhumbly named “ Trump accounts ”, calls for the federal government to give a one-time $1,000 seed deposit to every newborn whose family applies. In campaign speeches this summer , Trump has sought to milk these accounts for maximum political advantage, making big promises about how much these accounts will help the nation’s children.
